claims.text: A machine-learning-driven closed-loop synthesis platform can reliably produce noble-metal-based high-entropy-alloy three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
Closed-loop optimization of thermal, mixing, and atmospheric parameters improves atomic precision in NM-HEA nanoframework synthesis.
The starting materials are bulk NM-HEA precursors having diverse compositions and complex surface structures.
High-throughput in situ characterization and simulation data can provide feedback for dynamically adjusting NM-HEA synthesis parameters.
Thermal treatment, precursor mixing, and environmental conditions can be adjusted dynamically during synthesis.
Real-time feedback can be applied during early-stage NM-HEA nanostructure formation.
Atomic-scale decomposition and restructuring drive the formation of porous three-dimensional nanoframework morphologies.
Machine-learning algorithms can analyze real-time structural data to predict suitable processing-parameter adjustments.
Processing-parameter adjustments can precisely modulate nonlinear interactions and phase-decomposition dynamics in NM-HEAs.
Modulating phase-decomposition dynamics guides the self-assembly of atomic clusters into three-dimensional porous frameworks.
The proposed platform will produce NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframework catalysts with improved atomic control.
Nanoframeworks produced by the proposed platform will retain complex surface structures.
Improved atomic control and retention of complex surface structures may enhance catalytic performance.
Conventional static synthesis routes lack real-time feedback.
Conventional thermal treatments or static precursor-mixing routes do not achieve atomic-scale precision in porous NM-HEA nanostructure formation.
The approach is applicable only where high-throughput in situ characterization is feasible and decomposition or restructuring dynamics respond to feedback control.
